details:
Holoporting is extremely good and works very well as an alternative to teleportation, but the current artificial locomotion implementation leaves a little more to be desired.

Some toggles to enable various VR sickness reducing features would greatly improve the customization and accessibility of artificial locomotion and the VRChat play experience as a whole.

1. FOV Restriction, documented here:
http://www.cs.columbia.edu/2016/combating-vr-sickness/images/combating-vr-sickness.pdf
It does potentially reduce sense of presence, but that won't matter to people who just want to use artificial locomotion comfortably. This could also be applied to all forms of motion, to make jumping, falling, and moving chairs (vehicles, amusement park rides, Twin Drives and other flight variants etc) less sickness-inducing.

2. Inertia. Currently, locomotion is instant both to start and stop. Inertia can be used to alleviate VR sickness. This is also useful for players using headset-only VR setups (for example using VRidge or Trinus) who can only move with the keyboard, and thus always instantly move at full speed.

3. A toggle to disable non-forward movements. This way, it becomes impossible to accidentally move the Vive trackpad or Oculus analog stick in sickness-inducing sideways or backwards movements -- you would only be able to move forward in your head direction.

4. Reduced sensitivity and/or speed. As an Oculus Rift owner, I don't know how sensitive movement on the Vive trackpad (or by extension, the Windows MR trackpad) is, but I find that the analog stick sensitivity for movement on the Oculus Touch controllers is very high, and it doesn't help that the default speed in VR is always to run. Options for these would be very useful.

If there are any more suggestions, I would love to hear them.
title: Locomotion FOV restriction and inertia
